title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DARCY'S PHONE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Darcy, a crane operator from Grand Rapids, Michigan.
All day, she lifts steel beams, and never drops a thing.
But at home, one little phone was lifting her right out of her own life.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE GLOW
segments.quote: Men have become the tools of their tools.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: One summer night at dinner, her son Eli asked, Mom, can your phone pass the potatoes?
Darcy checked her screen time. Five hours a day.
Her husband Ben's old copy of Walden had one line underlined:
Men have become the tools of their tools.
The phone went to sleep in the kitchen drawer.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: ALL EARS
segments.quote: When people talk, listen completely. Most people never listen.
segments.author: Ernest Hemingway
lines: Eli started a long story about his best friend. Her hand drifted toward the drawer.
Then she remembered a sign in the job trailer, from Ernest Hemingway:
When people talk, listen completely. Most people never listen.
So she listened. His friend was moving away. Eli had been sad for weeks, and she'd missed it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE PORCH
segments.quote: It is impossible to enjoy idling thoroughly unless one has plenty of work to do.
segments.author: Jerome K. Jerome
lines: That Saturday, she kept patting her pocket, like she'd lost her keys.
Ben handed her an old book by Jerome K. Jerome, an English humorist:
It is impossible to enjoy idling thoroughly unless one has plenty of work to do.
Well, she worked fifty hours a week.
So she sat on the porch and did nothing. For a whole hour. Glorious.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: NO TIME
segments.quote: Dost thou love life? Then do not squander time, for that is the stuff life is made of.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: Then Eli asked to go fishing. Darcy said, I don't have time.
In the hallway hung Grandma's old cross-stitch, from Benjamin Franklin:
Dost thou love life? Then do not squander time, for that is the stuff life is made of.
Five hours a day. She had time. It was hiding in her pocket.
She blocked off Saturday mornings. In pen.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LIST
segments.quote: Besides the noble art of getting things done, there is the noble art of leaving things undone.
segments.author: Lin Yutang
lines: Her to-do list was a mile long. Gutters. Forty-two group texts.
Ben read her a line from Lin Yutang, a Chinese writer:
Besides the noble art of getting things done, there is the noble art of leaving things undone.
She crossed off half the list without doing any of it. The gutters survived.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LAKE
segments.quote: Summer afternoon, summer afternoon; to me those have always been the two most beautiful words in the English language.
segments.author: Henry James
lines: Saturday, the three of them sat on a dock, warm sun on the lake.
Eli caught a fish the size of a french fry, and cheered like it was a whale.
Darcy reached for her phone, then stopped. Ben quoted the novelist Henry James:
Summer afternoon, summer afternoon; to me those have always been the two most beautiful words in the English language.
No picture. She remembers it anyway.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Put it down. Listen fully. Rest. Make time. Leave some undone. Enjoy the afternoon.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Put the tool down. Listen all the way. Rest. Make time. Leave some things undone. Enjoy the afternoon.
I tried a selfie once. It's a lovely picture of my ear.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
